explanation: Dintero freezes only the outer Money/data containers, while amount() returns its retained Big object and getTags() returns its tag object. This demonstrates exposed aliases, not that every arithmetic operation mutates its operands.

The constructor copies input amount through new Big, then shallow-freezes two containers; accessors expose nested state. MONEY-ARITHMETIC-009 governs observed arithmetic operand preservation, so the alias mechanism is related ownership evidence rather than by itself a complete conformance failure.

A caller must mutate an exposed nested Big coefficient/tag value, or shared Big configuration must affect a later operation; ordinary reconstruction normally returns a new Money. explanation: ActualActualICMA can retain a mutable caller schedule, so future accrual uses the current schedule rather than a frozen snapshot.

The struct stores an AbstractVector and yearfrac reads schedule directly for first/last bounds, searches and denominator periods. The month StepRange convenience form is immutable, whereas a direct mutable-vector construction can change the subsequently read dates or introduce invalid ordering/zero periods. Core explicit-context principles motivate review but do not specify an ICMA schedule snapshot contract.

Construct with a mutable vector, retain its alias and change entries before a later yearfrac call. No mutation occurs inside yearfrac; callers that keep schedules stable avoid this issue. No correct replacement accrual formula or executed Julia outcome is asserted. Static review of the pinned bodies and prior attributed dependency contracts only; no upstream build, runtime outcome, deployed state or concurrency schedule was executed. This behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core.

evidence.title: Holiday-fact mutation and cache rebuild can change observable results
explanation: Holiday fact aliases can stale caches, and initcache! publishes changed bounds before rebuilt arrays.

GenericHolidayCalendar retains the Set; composite holiday checks traverse retained calendar references. needs_cache_update skips identical initialized bounds without fact versions. initcache! changes dtmin/dtmax before constructing arrays and does not replace hc; construction failure can leave new bounds with old arrays. Global initcache builds before replacing one dictionary entry but uses active calendar lookup; batch publication is sequential. Calendar caching has no own Core contract.

Mutate retained holiday facts then request identical bounds, or trigger rebuild failure after initcache! writes new bounds. No actual failed allocation, corrupt index or race was executed. Stable facts and successful fresh construction can behave normally. Static review of the pinned bodies and prior attributed dependency contracts only; no upstream build, runtime outcome, deployed state or concurrency schedule was executed. This behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core.

evidence.title: Chart helpers alter warning context for subsequent financial calls
explanation: Chart wrappers set global R warning policy and leave it changed for subsequent financial calls.

All four wrappers call options(warn=-1) without restoring the prior value on success or failure. wpr calls warning for weights not summing to one before computing the return. In the same R session the chart call can therefore suppress that later diagnostic. This is an ambient diagnostic side effect, not evidence that the computed Money value changed.

Call a chart wrapper in an R session then invoke a warning-producing financial helper without resetting options. No R session was executed; error conditions and numerical return are not transformed merely because warnings are suppressed. Static review of the pinned bodies and prior attributed dependency contracts only; no upstream build, runtime outcome, deployed state or concurrency schedule was executed. This behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core.

evidence.title: Mortality table caching exposes path identity and mutable table aliases
explanation: Mortality table cache is keyed by path and returns shared table objects; table collection keys can overwrite duplicate names.

readXTbML locks get! by the supplied path and reuses the cached object without content/mtime invalidation. Mortality vector wrappers can retain mutable arrays. read_tables constructs Dict pairs keyed by metadata.name without duplicate rejection. This motivates provenance/version and alias policies for actuarial tables, not a Core Money/cache requirement.

Reuse a path after external content change, mutate retained cached table rates, or load tables with duplicate metadata names. No file/table was mutated, and unchanged immutable usage is stable. Duplicate overwrite order depends on actual path enumeration. Static review of the pinned bodies and prior attributed dependency contracts only; no upstream build, runtime outcome, deployed state or concurrency schedule was executed. This behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core.

evidence.title: Revaluation retains established premium while textbook reserve reprices
explanation: PricedPolicy establishes equivalence premium once or accepts a finite supplied Real premium. Alternate valuation basis must keep original issue age/status/life order/contingency, while mortality and curve can change; rebase preserves product term/frequency/guarantee and policy_value subtracts the stored annualized premium. reserve_premium_net constructs a new equivalence premium on the supplied basis instead.
Source tests explicitly distinguish the APIs. Immutable wrapper does not freeze caller-owned mortality arrays or curves. No regulatory reserve method or independent actuarial correctness accepted.
